clue.text: Spooner's awful misty weather? Hearth's the place for one to be

definitions.text: Hearth's the place for one to be

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: something awful is dire
fog is misty weather

explanation.surface: A grumble about dreadful murky weather, followed by advice that the best place to sit it out is by the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the first letters of DIRE FOG to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, the metal support for logs in a fireplace, stands in the hearth.

clue.text: This person did the work and put on a false show, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is spoken and the entry sounds like it

parts.note: to fake it is to pretend or put on a false show

explanation.surface: Someone who did the job is accused of only pretending to.
explanation.walkthrough: Fecit, Latin for 'made it', is inscribed on artworks after the maker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'he or she made it', signed on a painting by its maker.

clue.text: Some err, wanting new direction — feeling this?

indicators.note: the words some err want to be pointed a new way, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: People who go wrong and wish to change course must feel regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is the guilt felt by those who have done wrong, which is what someone who errs should feel.

clue.text: Give up work, when under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue the work piece comes beneath the doctor piece

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: Someone stops working while being treated by a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a habit or plan is to abandon it, a synonym for give up.

clue.text: What to do for pre-match security? Look at the issues

definitions.text: What to do for pre-match security?
definitions.meaning: literally, to inspect the stadium ground before a match for security threats
figuratively, to review the matters in hand

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a literal inspection of the pitch and, idiomatically, a review of familiar points.

clue.text: Reveal peacekeepers wanting sudden improvement across society

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: the boom stretches across the society letter, so it encloses it

parts.note: a boom is a sudden upturn in trade

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers long for an economic upswing that spreads across the whole society.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbosom oneself is to confide or disclose one's feelings, so the verb means to reveal.

clue.text: Crusade going wrong with surprising lameness — do they want to put the clock back?

definitions.text: do they want to put the clock back?

indicators.note: the word crusade goes wrong and its letters are disordered
the word lameness is turned into something surprising by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A campaign fails because of an unexpected weakness, and its backers long for the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the clock back' is the shady trade of winding back a car's odometer to fake a low mileage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest second-hand car dealers are notorious for turning back mileage counters.

clue.text: Vessels, any number, in bay for time of celebration

indicators.note: the vessels and number sit in the bay word

parts.note: a bight is a wide curved bay
urns are vessels
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A number of boats moored in a bay for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns Night, 25 January, is the Scottish celebration of the poet Robert Burns with haggis and whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns Night is an annual evening of festivity, so a time of celebration.

clue.text: Thus Greek character's beginning to make specious argument

parts.note: so means thus
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, with 's as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Greek begins to make an argument that sounds plausible but is false.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophism is a clever but fallacious argument, like the Sophists used.

clue.text: Colouring matter — minute dash goes in

indicators.note: the dash goes into the minute abbreviation

parts.note: elan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: A hurried note about dye being added in a quick moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanin is the dark pigment in skin and hair, a natural colouring agent.

clue.text: Officer and ordinary soldiers locked in toilet

indicators.note: the soldiers are shut inside the toilet, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a commode is a chair concealing a chamber pot, a kind of toilet
OR stands for Other Ranks, the ordinary soldiers in the British army

explanation.surface: An officer and some privates have got themselves locked in the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rank above captain, so a senior officer.

clue.text: Force back partner's head in dance

indicators.note: the partner's first letter sits inside the dance word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: During a dance, someone pushes away their partner's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to drive it back, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Endless sweet cake is wrong

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the cake is dropped

parts.note: a torte is a rich sweet cake, often layered

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a never-ending gooey cake is a bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the final E from TORTE.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong, such as negligence, giving grounds for damages.

clue.text: What may produce bangs that could be supersonic

indicators.note: the letters of the word supersonic could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A remark about sonic booms from fast aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussion instruments such as drums and cymbals are struck to make bangs and crashes.

clue.text: Bed chamber?

parts.note: not a bedroom but a chamber lowered to the sea bed for underwater work

explanation.definitionFit: This open-bottomed chamber lets workers breathe while on the floor of the sea.

clue.text: Sun has to be demeaning to women?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
to exist is to be

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Sun newspaper is degrading to women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid long criticised for its topless Page 3 photographs, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexist behaviour discriminates against or belittles people on grounds of sex, typically women.

clue.text: Film in San Marino not so bad

indicators.note: bad means the remaining letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'not' says these two letters are removed from the country's name

explanation.surface: A film showing in San Marino turns out to be reasonably good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' removes S and O from SAN MARINO, leaving ANMARIN; 'bad' rearranges those. Rain Man is the 1988 film with Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain Man is a well-known Oscar-winning movie, so it is one example of a film.

clue.text: Liberal held in derision, making one cross

indicators.note: the Liberal letter is held inside the word for derision

parts.note: satire mocks and derides its targets
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician subjected to mockery is made angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: Old boy has hesitation during drink — needing to do this?

indicators.note: the old boy and hesitation come during the drink, so inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
er is a hesitating noise

explanation.surface: A former schoolmate hesitates over his drink, realising he needs to sober up.
explanation.definitionFit: Here 'this' points to the remedy a drinker needs, recovering from intoxication.

clue.text: Lecturer, a figure in mathematics, brief and to the point

parts.note: a conic is a curve formed by slicing a cone, a figure in geometry

explanation.surface: A maths lecturer's explanation is short and pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, terse and concise.

clue.text: Party order — two articles delivered outside

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the two articles are delivered around the outside of the order

parts.note: THE is the definite article
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone orders goods for a party and two items are left outside the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command but is the Order of Merit, a British honour; 'Party' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is an informal party or reception held in one's own house.

clue.text: One could create max. stir, maybe?

definitions.text: One could create max. stir, maybe?

indicators.note: the letters of max stir could create something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary might be expected to stir things up as much as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: a follower of Karl Marx is the kind of person who might stir up revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Marx's revolutionary doctrine is a likely agitator.

clue.text: Where you may find shrubs pruned raggedly — just some!

parts.note: just some letters of these two words, read right to left, give a word for a plot of cultivated ground

explanation.surface: A gardener's note that some shrubs have been hacked about untidily.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse hidden clue: read as an instruction, 'garden, back' means GARDEN reversed, NEDRAG, which is 'just some' of 'pruNED RAGgedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrubs and lawns are typically planted in the garden behind a house.

clue.text: Weary one falling before end of walk — a long one

indicators.note: the one drops away from the word for weary

parts.note: to weary is to tire
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tired walker collapses before finishing a lengthy hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' drops I from TIRE, leaving TRE; 'end of walk' adds K.
explanation.definitionFit: Here 'one' stands for walk, and a trek is a long, arduous journey on foot.

clue.text: Praise message of indifference to nation? The reverse!

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the whole message backwards

parts.note: sod it is a dismissive message of not caring
the UK is a nation

explanation.surface: A message saying the country does not care, when the opposite is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns SOD UK backwards; the surface pretends it means the opposite meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is acclaim or prestige, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Puff? Puff perhaps, when legless

indicators.note: the on side is the leg side in cricket, so the leg letters are removed

parts.note: Puff the Magic Dragon from the folk song is an example of a dragon

explanation.surface: Someone takes a puff of a cigarette while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the on side is also called the leg side, so 'legless' strips ON from DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is an inhalation on a cigarette, the same as a puff.

clue.text: Compass shows north, needed in storm

indicators.note: north is needed inside the storm word, so it goes within it

parts.note: to storm is to rage
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A navigator's compass reads north, which is needed in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent, the full span covered, is a synonym of range.

clue.text: Single island in setting that's not spoilt

indicators.note: the island is placed in the setting formed by the other piece

parts.note: unmarred describes something not spoilt or damaged

explanation.surface: A single island in an unspoilt natural setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone single has no spouse, so has never wed.

clue.text: Best man seen round back of hotel, drunk

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: The best man at a wedding is seen behind the hotel, the worse for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' looks like the wedding role but is two pieces; 'seen round' just has the man come round after the hotel's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal slang for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Denies entrance into cosy home, when time has passed

indicators.note: time has gone away, so the letter for time drops out
the entrance goes into the cosy home word

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone refuses entry to a snug house because it is too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts GATE in NEST to give NEGATEST; 'when time has passed' then removes the T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or contradict it.
